title: Practice 1: Running, swimming, climbing, crawling, dragging

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: A rabbit is running in the garden.
exercises.why: **бегает** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **бегать** (to run) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **бежать** for one direction. present: я бе́гаю · ты бе́гаешь · он бе́гает · мы бе́гаем · вы бе́гаете · они бе́гают. — Wiktionary, «бегать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs бегать-бежать, побежать belong to the group of "going verbs" similar to the verbs ходить-идти, пойти.» — DLI, Lesson 82.  «по саду» — movement in various directions, not towards one goal.  The other choice: **бежит** is from **бежать**, the one-direction verb.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite). (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Can chimpanzees swim?
exercises.why: **плавать** (the infinitive) (to swim, to float) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **плыть** for one direction. — Wiktionary, «плавать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verb плавать — плыть, поплыть belong to the group of "going verbs" similar to the verbs ходить — идти, пойти; "плавать" (like "ходить") is a "repeated function" verb. Note the ways in which it is used: Я умею плавать. — I know how to swim. Дерево плавает в воде. — Wood floats in water. Я плаваю на этом корабле. — I sail (work) on this ship. In naval terminology the verb "идти" instead of "плыть" is commonly used: Я иду на этом корабле. Наш корабль идёт по Чёрному морю. Мы шли в Архангельск.» — DLI, Lesson 73.  «умеют» speaks of ability or liking — general motion, again the many-directions verb.  Compare: «Птицы летают, рыбы плавают, а собаки ходят.» (Birds fly, fish swim, and dogs walk.) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **плыть** is from **плыть**, the one-direction verb.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

(Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The dog was running toward him.
exercises.why: **бежала** is the past tense (feminine) of **бежать** ((imperfective only) to run, to be running) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **бегать** for many directions. past: он бежа́л · она бежа́ла · оно бежа́ло · они бежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «бежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Unidirectional verbs describe motion in progress in one direction.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs бегать-бежать, побежать belong to the group of "going verbs" similar to the verbs ходить-идти, пойти. Note that in the conjugation of the verb "бежать", the consonants "ж" and "г" are alternated: я бегу, ты бежишь, они бегут. Note also that in all persons, except the 3rd person plural, it belongs to the 2nd conjugation: ты бежишь, он бежит, мы бежим, вы бежите. In the 3rd person plural it belongs to the 1st conjugation: они бегут.» — DLI, Lesson 82.  «навстречу» gives a direction or a moment: one way, in progress, so the one-direction verb.  The other choice: **бегала** is from **бегать**, the many-directions verb.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: The antelope runs extremely fast.
exercises.why: **бегают** is the present tense (3rd person plural) of **бегать** (to run) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **бежать** for one direction. present: я бе́гаю · ты бе́гаешь · он бе́гает · мы бе́гаем · вы бе́гаете · они бе́гают. — Wiktionary, «бегать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Multidirectional verbs describe: 1. General motion, referring to ability or habitual motion, without reference to direction or destination; 2. Movement in various directions; 3. Repetition of completed trips; 4. In the past tense, a single completed round trip.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs бегать-бежать, побежать belong to the group of "going verbs" similar to the verbs ходить-идти, пойти.» — DLI, Lesson 82.  The other choice: **бегут** is from **бежать**, the one-direction verb.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Unprefixed verbs of motion, which are all imperfective, divide into pairs based on the direction of the movement (uni- or multidirectional — sometimes referred to as determinate/indeterminate or definite/indefinite). (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))
